Q: Situations where R strips attributes for S3 classes, and how to work around or avoid them? A:

Though slightly off-topic, if you want to learn about S4 and work with tiny numbers, take a look at contributed package Brobdingnag. Its vignette("S4_brob", package = "Brobdingnag") is one f the best introductions to writing S4 classes I've seen and the package deals with numeric S4 objects storing log(x) (natural log) and sign(x). This allows for very large or very small numbers arithmetic.
As an example,

library(Brobdingnag)
#> Loading required package: Matrix
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'Brobdingnag'
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:Matrix':
#> 
#>     diag, t
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:base':
#> 
#>     diag, t

make_brob <- function(txt_pvals) {
  as.brob(as.numeric(txt_pvals))
}

# brobs' slots are atomic vectors so base::ifelse works
ifelse_brob <- function(test, yes, no) {
  stopifnot(is.brob(yes), is.brob(no))
  # create a brob object and return to caller
  brob(
    x = ifelse(test, yes@x, no@x),
    positive = ifelse(test, yes@positive, no@positive)
  )
}

A <- c('4e-40','3.6e-150','1.9e-250')
a <- make_brob(A)
a
#> [1] +exp(-90.717) +exp(-344.11) +exp(-575)

# original and the brob are not equal, there
# is a precision loss, see the package docs
as.numeric(a) ==  as.numeric(A)
#> [1] FALSE FALSE FALSE
as.numeric(a) -  as.numeric(A)
#> [1]   8.972294e-55  7.325987e-164 -1.767741e-264
all.equal(as.numeric(a),  as.numeric(A))
#> [1] TRUE

B <- c('1.5e-90','2.1e-230','9.5e-60')
b <- make_brob(B)
b
#> [1] +exp(-206.83) +exp(-528.85) +exp(-135.9)
as.numeric(b)
#> [1]  1.5e-90 2.1e-230  9.5e-60

test <- c(F, F, T)
ifelse_brob(test, a, b)
#> [1] +exp(-206.83) +exp(-528.85) +exp(-575)

# it will recycle, just like base::ifelse
test2 <- c(F, F, T, T, T)
ifelse_brob(test2, a, b)
#> [1] +exp(-206.83) +exp(-528.85) +exp(-575)    +exp(-90.717) +exp(-344.11)

Q: SQL Query to Filter Rows Above Average While Removing Consecutive Qualifying Rows A:

SELECT id, A

FROM (

SELECT 

    \*,

    LAG(A \>= avg_a) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS prev_ok

FROM (

    SELECT \*, AVG(A) OVER () AS avg_a

    FROM my_table

) t

) x

WHERE A >= avg_a

AND (prev_ok IS NULL OR prev_o

k = FALSE);

Q: How to read/write in minio using spark? A:

“The question asks how to read/write files from MinIO using Spark. The error hostname cannot be null occurs because Spark cannot resolve the bucket hostname in the S3A URL. The accepted answer works by correctly configuring the Spark session: setting the spark.hadoop.fs.s3a.endpoint to the MinIO host, enabling path.style.access, and disabling SSL for HTTP connections. This allows Spark to communicate with the MinIO bucket and read/write files successfully. The accepted answer ensures the Docker container network and hostnames are correctly resolved so Spark can access the bucket.”

Q: Dart mqtt_client identifierRejected and a disconnection origin of none A:

I was facing the same issue. In my case, I had to modify the Security Policy to allow connection (by default it was only allowing the Java and NodeJs SDks, and simple basicPubSub):

  • AWS IoT Core console

  • Manage Security

  • Policies -> select your policy

  • Edit Active Version

  • set iot:Connect to *

  • manually activate new policy version
